author: Reagan Hillman
title: Police injured in Brockport arrest of man with felony warrant - NewsBreak
text:
By Reagan Hillman ,
5 hours ago
BROCKPORT, N.Y. (WROC) — A man in Brockport is facing multiple charges after a traffic stop developed into a physical altercation with police during an arrest.
On the morning of August 22, Brockport Police stopped a white van on Fair Street for multiple offenses. The officer then learned that the driver was allegedly under the influence, had a suspended license, and had a felony warrant out of Ontario County.
As officers tried to arrest Juan J. Galvez-Perez, the 26-year-old allegedly tried to flee and then resisted arrest by fighting and biting officers.
Galvez-Perez was charged with second-degree assault with intent to injure a police officer, DWI (previous conviction), second-degree criminal impersonation, resisting arrest, obstruction of governmental administration, and multiple traffic violations, including aggravated unlicensed operation in the first, second, and third degrees.
More charges may be filed. The investigation is ongoing.
The officers suffered minor injuries; they were treated and released from the hospital.
Galvez-Perez was taken to the Monroe County Jail, where he was arraigned and held on a $5,000 bail or $20,000 bond. He is being held on a felony warrant from Ontario County for failing to appear in a possession-of-a-weapon case.
